sources.entry: Tinyproxy - Light-weight HTTP/HTTPS proxy daemon. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 C/deb

summary.one_liner: Tinyproxy is a small, efficient HTTP/HTTPS proxy daemon written in C and released under the GPL.
summary.what_it_does: Tinyproxy is a lightweight HTTP/SSL proxy daemon intended for small networks where a larger proxy would be too resource intensive or a security risk. It buffers high-speed responses from servers and relays them to clients at the speed the client accepts, which the README says reduces sluggishness when sharing an Internet connection. The build uses a standard GNU configure/automake process. Optional build-time features include debug support, an XTinyproxy header, domain and URL filtering, upstream proxy chaining, transparent proxying (works when traffic is redirected by firewall rules), reverse proxying, and a configurable stats host name.
use_cases: share an internet connection with a small network
restrict a small network to HTTP and HTTPS traffic
run a lightweight forward proxy on a home or office server
filter domains and URLs through a proxy
chain traffic through an upstream proxy
set up a transparent or reverse proxy
how_to_run: ./autogen.sh (only when building from a git checkout)
notable: Buffers server responses and relays them to clients at the client's maximum speed
Optional compile-time modules for filtering, upstream proxying, transparent and reverse proxy modes
Designed as a small, low-resource alternative to larger proxy servers
Listed in awesome-selfhosted under Proxy, with a deb package noted
caveats: Optional features such as filtering, upstream, transparent and reverse proxy must be enabled at compile time
Transparent mode depends on firewall redirection rules configured outside Tinyproxy
README describes it as suited to small networks rather than large-scale deployments
